To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a novel early light-induced gene in rice, that the gene is induced by both R and FR light, that the gene shows a high degree of similarity to Arabidopsis lipase 1 and that we found the gene to be rapidly induced in rice by jasmonic acid.
we identified a new early-light and JA-induced gene, which encodes an enzyme that may act as a negative regulator for light-induced coleoptile elongations.
a novel early light-and JA-induced gene, GER1, was isolated and characterized, and that this gene may be involved in light- and JA-signalling pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new gene that may be involved in the light/JA interaction.
a new class of GDSL motif-containing enzymes, the function of which is not known.
a novel early light-induced gene that is regulated by both R and FR light.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light-induced biosynthesis of jasmonates in rice is not only important for photomorphogenesis, but also plays a role in the control of plant defence responses.
the HEBIBAs mutant phenotype is caused by the loss of a negative regulator of light signalling that is induced by both light and JA.
light and JA signalling converge at the level of a GDSL motif-containing gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HEBIBAs mutant phenotype results from a defect in JA biosynthesis, that the light response in coleoptiles is regulated by JA, that the light and JA responses converge on a common pathway and that the convergence point is regulated by a GDSL motif-containing gene.
the light-induced biosynthesis of JA is required to inhibit the light-induced growth response of coleoptile tissue in rice seedlings.

the light-induced biosynthesis of JA is essential for the inhibition of coleoptile growth in rice, and that GER1 is a novel light-induced gene that is involved in the light-triggering of the JA biosynthesis pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HEBIBa rice mutant can be used to identify genes that are specifically regulated by light and jasmonate.
we have identified a new gene that responds to both red light and jasmonate.
the light and JA pathways converge at least partially on GER1, a gene that is rapidly induced by R and FR light and JA.
